diagnostic_evidence.quote: Suppose further that for every $n = 0,1,\ldots,N_t-1$, (\ref{root}) has a root and that $A_n$ as well as $E_n$ are finite.

issues.failure_explanation: The corollaries refer to $A$, $E$ (and $A_n$, $E_n$) as if they were defined in their context, but these quantities are defined in Theorem stab_thm and Theorem stab_cont in terms of the exact solution and a perturbed solution $(\bar\rho,\bar c)$ and residual $R_{\bar\rho}$. The corollaries only introduce a reconstruction $\tilde\rho$ and do not define $\bar\rho$, $\bar c$, or $R_{\bar\rho}$. Thus the conditions in the corollaries are not well-defined and cannot be verified as stated.

failure_location.quote: Suppose further that (\ref{stab_cond}) is satisfied and that $A$ as well as $E$ are finite.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Explicitly set $\bar\rho = \tilde\rho$, $\bar c = \tilde c$, and define $R_{\bar\rho}$ as the residual of the reconstruction (as done later in Theorem main_thm), and state that $A$, $E$ (or $A_n$, $E_n$) are the corresponding quantities.
issues.overall_effect: The a posteriori verifiable existence corollaries are ill-posed as written; the reader cannot check the stated conditions.
issues.title: Undefined constants in a posteriori existence corollaries
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local addition of definitions; it does not require new mathematical arguments or change the substantive claims.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we obtain the local-in-time estimate \begin{align*} \sup_{t \in [t^n,t^{n+1}]}\norm{e(t,\cdot)}_{L^2}^2 +  \int_{t^n}^{t^{n+1}} \left| e(t,\cdot) \right|_{H^1}^2 dt \leq \delta_n A_n E_n, \end{align*} for all $n = 0, 1, \ldots, N_t-1$

issues.failure_explanation: The derivation establishes only local estimates on each time interval $[t^n,t^{n+1}]$. The global integral over $[0,T]$ is the sum of the local integrals, so it is bounded by the sum $\sum_{n=0}^{N_t-1} \Psi_n$ (plus the maximum of the local sup bounds for the global sup). The theorem instead claims the global sup plus integral is bounded by $\Psi_{N_t-1}$, which is only the last local bound. Since $\Psi_n > 0$, this is generally much smaller than the sum and is false.

failure_location.quote: Then, provided (\ref{root}) has a root for all $n = 0, 1, \ldots, N_t-1$, it holds \begin{align*} &\sup_{t \in [0,T]}\norm{\rho(t,\cdot) - \bar{\rho}(t,\cdot)}_{L^2}^2 +  \int_0^T \left| \rho(t,\cdot) - \bar{\rho}(t,\cdot) \right|_{H^1}^2 dt \leq \Psi_{N_t-1}, \end{align*}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the final bound by the sum of the local bounds, e.g. $\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\|e\|^2 + \int_0^T |e|^2 \le \sum_{n=0}^{N_t-1} \Psi_n$ (or a similar cumulative bound), and propagate this correction to Theorem main_thm (ii) and Corollary cor:added-2.
issues.overall_effect: The local-in-time continuation stability estimate and the a posteriori error estimator in Theorem main_thm (ii) are invalid as stated; the guaranteed error bound is understated.
issues.title: Global stability bound incorrectly uses only the last local estimate
issues.why_classification: The error is in the central global stability statement. The correct bound involves a sum over time steps, which materially changes the guaranteed estimate and affects the main a posteriori error estimator.

issues.failure_explanation: The Keller-Segel system and the existence theorem assume only $\rho_0 \in L^2$. An $L^2$ function is not defined pointwise, so the evaluation $\rho_0(x_K)$ at cell centers $x_K$ is not well-defined for general initial data.

failure_location.quote: We start by defining $\rho_h^0 \in R_h$ by $\rho_h^0|_K := \rho_0(x_K)$, for all $K \in\mathcal{T}_h$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the initial cell values by local averages, e.g. $\rho_h^0|_K := \frac{1}{|K|}\int_K \rho_0 \,dx$, or assume additional regularity (e.g. $\rho_0 \in C(\bar\Omega)$) for the point evaluation.
issues.overall_effect: The algorithm is not well-defined for the stated class of initial data, so the numerical approximation cannot be computed as described for arbitrary $\rho_0 \in L^2$.
issues.title: Algorithm initialization requires point evaluation of an $L^2$ datum
issues.why_classification: The fix is a short, local change to the initialization (cell averages) and does not affect the rest of the scheme or the main convergence framework.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Further, let $(\bar{\rho},\bar{c})$ with $\bar{\rho} \in C(0,T;H^1)$, $\partial_t \bar{\rho} \in C(0,T;H^{-1})$ and $\bar{c} \in C(0,T;H^2)$ be a solution to the perturbed system

issues.failure_explanation: The stability theorems (Theorem stab_thm and Theorem stab_cont) require the perturbed solution to have time derivative continuous in time, specifically $\partial_t \bar{\rho} \in C(0,T;H^{-1})$. The reconstruction $\tilde{\rho}$ is only piecewise linear in time; its time derivative is piecewise constant and has jump discontinuities at the time nodes. Hence $\partial_t \tilde{\rho} \notin C(0,T;H^{-1})$, so the reconstruction does not satisfy the hypotheses of the stability theorems. Applying these theorems to $(\tilde{\rho},\tilde{c})$ in Theorem main_thm (and in the corollaries) is therefore not justified as written.

failure_location.quote: Let $(\rho,c)$ be a weak solution of the Keller-Segel system (\ref{KS1}), (\ref{KS2}), (\ref{KScond}) and let $(\tilde{\rho},\tilde{c})$ be the reconstruction of our numerical approximation defined in \autoref{Morley}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either relax the regularity assumptions in the stability theorems to allow piecewise continuous time derivatives (e.g. $\partial_t \bar{\rho} \in L^\infty(0,T;H^{-1})$ or piecewise continuous) and verify the proofs still hold, or modify the temporal reconstruction to be continuously differentiable in time (e.g. by a smooth interpolation) while preserving the residual estimates.
issues.overall_effect: The main a posteriori error estimators in Theorem main_thm and the a posteriori existence corollaries are not rigorously supported, because the stability frameworks cannot be applied to the constructed reconstruction under the stated regularity assumptions.
issues.title: Reconstruction lacks required temporal regularity for stability theorems
issues.why_classification: This invalidates the application of the central stability results to the reconstruction, which is the foundation of the main a posteriori error estimator. The repair requires either re-proving the stability theorems under weaker regularity or changing the reconstruction, both of which are substantive.
